newsitem.title: USA: Phillips says U.S. Gulf Mahogany field restart Fri.
newsitem.headline: Phillips says U.S. Gulf Mahogany field restart Fri.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said it will restart one of two producing wells at the offshore Louisiana Mahogany field later Friday.
The wells were shut down two weeks ago after ice plugs formed in tubing as a result of frozen hydrocarbons.
Phillips spokesman Rob Phillips said production would not return to full capacity immediately, and could not give an expected production level from the return of the one well.
"One well will go back up today, and the timing for the second well is not known," Phillips said.
Mahogany is expected to see average 1997 production rates of 22,000 barrels per day of oil and 30 million cubic feet of natgas per day.
Phillips said Mahogany wells were running at test rates and, as a result, hindered an accurate flow count.
The field is the first subsalt production in the Gulf of Mexico.
